core.title: A topology-constrained multimodal LLM agent for fault diagnosis in highway electromechanical systems
core.venue: International Conference on Computer Vision, Robotics and Automation Engineering
core.abstract: Highway electromechanical systems contain heterogeneous equipment such as lane controllers, license plate recognition cameras, barriers, switches, UPS units, power distribution cabinets, servers, sensors, and operation platforms. In daily maintenance, a visible service interruption may originate from power supply degradation, network instability, single-device failure, inter-device collaboration errors, or system-level configuration changes. This paper proposes a topology-constrained multimodal large language model (LLM) agent framework for evidence-based fault diagnosis and human-in-the-loop maintenance decision support. The framework integrates asset records, device states, alarms, work orders, lane business events, environmental measurements, and transient electrical signals. Two complementary topologies are constructed: a physical infrastructure topology for power, network, cabinet, and device dependencies, and a business collaboration topology for lane-side event chains and platform services. Based on the dual topology, the system builds a structured diagnostic evidence package that is used by an LLM agent for root-cause ranking, evidence explanation, maintenance recommendation, and work-order drafting. Experiments are conducted on an anonymized highway electromechanical maintenance dataset. Compared with rule-based diagnosis, text-only retrieval-augmented generation, structured classifier, and graph-based classifiers, the proposed method improves fault classification, root-cause localization, and recommendation acceptance rate. The results indicate that topology constraints and multimodal evidence packaging can constrain diagnostic reasoning with explicit evidence and make LLM agents more reliable for highway electromechanical maintenance.

sections.title: 服务中断背后，故障可能跨越设备边界
paragraphs: 高速公路机电系统包含车道控制器、车牌识别摄像机、栏杆机、交换机、UPS、配电柜及平台等异构设备。同样表现为服务中断，背后可能是供电退化、网络不稳定、单设备故障，也可能涉及设备协作错误或系统配置变化。诊断因此不仅要识别异常设备，还要辨析设备依赖与业务协作关系。

sections.title: 用物理依赖与业务协作组织诊断证据
paragraphs: 框架整合资产记录、设备状态、告警、工单、车道业务事件、环境测量和暂态电信号，并构建互补的双重拓扑：物理基础设施拓扑描述供电、网络、机柜和设备依赖；业务协作拓扑描述车道侧事件链与平台服务。
系统基于双重拓扑构建结构化诊断证据包，供大语言模型智能体开展根因排序、证据解释、维护建议和工单草拟。摘要将其定位为**人在回路的维护决策支持**，而非无需人工参与的自动维修系统。

sections.title: 摘要报告分类、定位与建议接受率改善
paragraphs: 研究在匿名化的高速公路机电运维数据集上开展实验。摘要报告，相比规则诊断、纯文本检索增强生成、结构化分类器和图分类器，该方法改善了故障分类、根因定位和建议接受率。

core.title: Large Language Models for Wind Turbine Fault Diagnosis: A Review of Enabling Technologies, Component-Level Applications, and Future Perspectives
core.abstract: Wind turbine fault diagnosis (WTFD) requires combining heterogeneous measurements with engineering knowledge under changing operating conditions. Large language models (LLMs) are being investigated for numerical diagnosis, inspection interpretation, and diagnostic decision support, but these roles have different evidence requirements. This structured narrative review examines enabling technologies and component-level applications for hub and blades, gearboxes, bearings, and generators. Explicit review questions guide a consolidated evidence map linking components, tasks, data modalities, model roles, and validation maturity. Individual study summaries distinguish direct research evidences, related-domain demonstrations, and proposed implementation pathways. Comparisons show why results from feature selection, adapted numerical prediction, knowledge retrieval, and report generation cannot be interpreted as interchangeable diagnostic capabilities. Furthermore, the discussion addresses unsuccessful retrieval configurations, possible temporal leakage, unverified explanations, and the gap between retrospective field-data evaluation and operational deployment. This review offers researchers a conceptual roadmap and practitioners a reference for evaluating the readiness of LLM-based diagnostic tools in operational wind energy environments.

core.title: Panoramic: A Cross-Layer Measurement Platform for Open RAN Deployments
core.venue: Proceedings of the 3rd ACM Workshop on Open and AI RAN
core.abstract: Open RAN deployments produce telemetry from the RAN, 5G core, Kubernetes, servers, fronthaul switches, and radio units, but each source uses a different identity model. The RAN identifies activity by cell-ID and PCI, Kubernetes by namespace and pod, switches by port and VLAN. Existing tools collect these sources separately and provide no common mapping between their identifiers, so correlating a DU event with a host CPU spike or a switch-port error requires manual topology reconstruction for every query. Within a single source, metrics do not always carry enough identifiers to determine which component or deployment they belong to. We present Panoramic, a measurement platform that addresses this gap and builds the missing mapping from the deployment configuration and attaches it to metrics at the time of ingestion. Source-specific collectors preserve the original KPI semantics while adding shared tags that make measurements from different layers joinable. Stable deployment identifiers remain always on; transient runtime identifiers such as RNTIs and pod names are enabled only when RAN is operational, keeping routine monitoring lightweight. Panoramic supports cross-layer fault diagnosis, dataset export for machine-learning applications, and bounded agentic operation in which a language-model agent diagnoses faults and executes approved actions through an interface constrained by role-based access control (RBAC).

core.abstract: The article examines modern methods for predicting the remaining life of metallic ship structures with due consideration of fatigue, crack growth, corrosion wastage, and actual operating conditions. The analytical basis comprises eleven peer-reviewed publications issued in 2021–2026 and three regulatory and technical documents published by IMO and DNV. Fracture mechanics, fatigue-life prediction, finite element analysis, corrosion prediction, structural health monitoring, and artificial-intelligence-based methods are compared. It is established that the reliability of a remaining-life assessment depends on the joint consideration of the measured structural condition, the model of subsequent degradation, future loading, and the applicable limit-state criterion. The most substantiated direction of further development is the integration of physics-based and probabilistic models with monitoring data and computational prediction tools.

core.title: The influence of flow-field representation on electrical power and fatigue-load surrogate modelling in offshore wind farms
core.abstract: High-fidelity aeroelastic simulations provide accurate predictions of electrical power and structural fatigue loads in wind farms but remain computationally expensive for optimisation, control, and digital-twin applications. Machine-learning surrogate models offer an efficient alternative, and recent studies have shown that both surrogate architecture and inflow representation influence predictive performance. However, it remains unclear how the amount and form of retained rotor-plane inflow information affect electrical power and fatigue-load prediction. This study evaluates four input configurations derived from temporally aggregated rotor-plane inflow data from the publicly available HAWC2Farm Lillgrund dataset. A minimal baseline representation retains only the spatial averages of the temporal-mean wind-speed and temporal-variance fields, while a flattened full-grid representation retains all rotor-plane measurements. Principal component analysis (PCA) provides a compact representation of the full input, and a two-dimensional representation preserves the original rotor-plane topology. The baseline, flattened, and PCA configurations are compared using the same SimpleMLP architecture under 5-fold GroupKFold cross-validation, while the two-dimensional spatial representation is evaluated separately using a convolutional neural network as a topology-aware modelling configuration. For electrical power prediction, the two-variable baseline already retained most of the predictive information, achieving an RMSE of approximately 2.2 % of rated power, while the distributed representations further reduced the absolute prediction error. For fatigue-load prediction, the effect of distributed inflow information was substantially more load-channel dependent, with only a marginal difference for tower-base fore–aft bending but much larger differences for blade-root edgewise and main-bearing bending. Within the fixed-architecture comparison, the PCA representation achieved the highest accuracy for electrical power prediction while reducing the input dimensionality from 1800 variables to 128 principal components. In contrast, the topology-aware CNN achieved the lowest prediction errors across all 12 fatigue-load components. These results show that the value of distributed rotor-plane information differs between the two prediction tasks and that the most effective representation–architecture configuration among those evaluated depends on the prediction objective.

papers.title: A topology-constrained multimodal LLM agent for fault diagnosis in highway electromechanical systems
papers.venue: International Conference on Computer Vision, Robotics and Automation Engineering
papers.abstract: Highway electromechanical systems contain heterogeneous equipment such as lane controllers, license plate recognition cameras, barriers, switches, UPS units, power distribution cabinets, servers, sensors, and operation platforms. In daily maintenance, a visible service interruption may originate from power supply degradation, network instability, single-device failure, inter-device collaboration errors, or system-level configuration changes. This paper proposes a topology-constrained multimodal large language model (LLM) agent framework for evidence-based fault diagnosis and human-in-the-loop maintenance decision support. The framework integrates asset records, device states, alarms, work orders, lane business events, environmental measurements, and transient electrical signals. Two complementary topologies are constructed: a physical infrastructure topology for power, network, cabinet, and device dependencies, and a business collaboration topology for lane-side event chains and platform services. Based on the dual topology, the system builds a structured diagnostic evidence package that is used by an LLM agent for root-cause ranking, evidence explanation, maintenance recommendation, and work-order drafting. Experiments are conducted on an anonymized highway electromechanical maintenance dataset. Compared with rule-based diagnosis, text-only retrieval-augmented generation, structured classifier, and graph-based classifiers, the proposed method improves fault classification, root-cause localization, and recommendation acceptance rate. The results indicate that topology constraints and multimodal evidence packaging can constrain diagnostic reasoning with explicit evidence and make LLM agents more reliable for highway electromechanical maintenance.

papers.title: Large Language Models for Wind Turbine Fault Diagnosis: A Review of Enabling Technologies, Component-Level Applications, and Future Perspectives
papers.abstract: Wind turbine fault diagnosis (WTFD) requires combining heterogeneous measurements with engineering knowledge under changing operating conditions. Large language models (LLMs) are being investigated for numerical diagnosis, inspection interpretation, and diagnostic decision support, but these roles have different evidence requirements. This structured narrative review examines enabling technologies and component-level applications for hub and blades, gearboxes, bearings, and generators. Explicit review questions guide a consolidated evidence map linking components, tasks, data modalities, model roles, and validation maturity. Individual study summaries distinguish direct research evidences, related-domain demonstrations, and proposed implementation pathways. Comparisons show why results from feature selection, adapted numerical prediction, knowledge retrieval, and report generation cannot be interpreted as interchangeable diagnostic capabilities. Furthermore, the discussion addresses unsuccessful retrieval configurations, possible temporal leakage, unverified explanations, and the gap between retrospective field-data evaluation and operational deployment. Prioritised research directions connect these uncertainties to matched ablations, validation, and prospective field studies. This review offers researchers a conceptual roadmap and practitioners a reference for evaluating the readiness of LLM-based diagnostic tools in operational wind energy environments.

article.lead: 大语言模型能否用于风机故障诊断，关键不只是能否生成答案，而是答案背后具有什么证据。这篇综述梳理不同部件、任务与模型角色，帮助读者区分“能够辅助某个环节”与“已具备可部署的诊断能力”。

sections.title: 风机诊断需要的不只是语言答案
paragraphs: 风机故障诊断需要在变化的运行工况下，将异构测量数据与工程知识结合起来。大语言模型正被探索用于数值诊断、巡检解读和诊断决策支持，但这些任务并不共享同一套证据要求。理解它们各自承担什么角色，是判断工具价值的前提。

sections.title: 用证据图谱连接部件、任务与验证成熟度
paragraphs: 本文是一篇结构化叙述性综述，覆盖轮毂与叶片、齿轮箱、轴承和发电机的相关使能技术及部件级应用。作者以明确的综述问题引导综合证据图谱，将部件、任务、数据模态、模型角色和验证成熟度联系起来。
在单项研究的梳理中，综述区分直接研究证据、相关领域演示以及拟议实施路径。这种组织方式保留了证据来源与成熟程度的差别，避免把尚处于构想阶段的应用与已经报告的研究结果混为一谈。

sections.title: 不同任务的成绩不能兑换成同一种诊断能力
paragraphs: 摘要报告的核心比较结论是：特征选择、适配后的数值预测、知识检索和报告生成，其结果不能被视为可相互替代的诊断能力。**完成一个辅助任务，不等于证明整个故障诊断流程可靠。**阅读相关成果时，需要先确认模型究竟完成了哪类任务。
综述还讨论了未成功的检索配置、可能存在的时间泄漏、未经验证的解释，以及现场数据回顾性评估与实际运行部署之间的差距。这些是文中讨论的风险与证据缺口，并不意味着所有被综述的方法都存在同样问题。

sections.title: 摘要不足以判定具体方法的部署水平
paragraphs: 仅凭摘要，无法判断纳入研究的数量、样本规模、数据来源与工况覆盖，也无法核对具体模型、比较基线、评价指标及验证划分。摘要未给出各类方法的量化结果，因此不能据此排序模型性能，或断言某种方案已经适用于现场部署。
摘要提到将相关不确定性与匹配的消融比较、验证及前瞻性现场研究相联系，但没有提供这些工作的具体实施与结果。这属于综述提出的研究方向，不能解读为作者已经完成了相应验证。

paragraphs: 阅读启发：面向智能运维应用，可沿着本文的证据图谱继续追问：模型处理的是数值数据、巡检内容还是知识检索？结论来自风机领域的直接证据，还是相关领域演示？解释是否经过验证，回顾性结果又如何支撑运行部署？这些问题比笼统询问“大模型是否有效”更有助于理解研究边界。

papers.title: Panoramic: A Cross-Layer Measurement Platform for Open RAN Deployments
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 3rd ACM Workshop on Open and AI RAN
papers.abstract: Open RAN deployments produce telemetry from the RAN, 5G core, Kubernetes, servers, fronthaul switches, and radio units, but each source uses a different identity model. The RAN identifies activity by cell-ID and PCI, Kubernetes by namespace and pod, switches by port and VLAN. Existing tools collect these sources separately and provide no common mapping between their identifiers, so correlating a DU event with a host CPU spike or a switch-port error requires manual topology reconstruction for every query. Within a single source, metrics do not always carry enough identifiers to determine which component or deployment they belong to. We present Panoramic, a measurement platform that addresses this gap and builds the missing mapping from the deployment configuration and attaches it to metrics at the time of ingestion. Source-specific collectors preserve the original KPI semantics while adding shared tags that make measurements from different layers joinable. Stable deployment identifiers remain always on; transient runtime identifiers such as RNTIs and pod names are enabled only when RAN is operational, keeping routine monitoring lightweight. Panoramic supports cross-layer fault diagnosis, dataset export for machine-learning applications, and bounded agentic operation in which a language-model agent diagnoses faults and executes approved actions through an interface constrained by role-based access control (RBAC).

sections.title: 同一套部署，各层却使用不同标识
paragraphs: Open RAN 部署的遥测来自无线接入网、5G 核心网、Kubernetes、服务器、前传交换机和无线单元。它们并不共享统一的身份模型：无线接入网使用 cell-ID 和 PCI，Kubernetes 使用命名空间和 pod，交换机则使用端口和 VLAN。
因此，把多个来源的数据采集起来，并不意味着已经能够跨层关联。摘要指出，现有工具分别采集这些来源，却没有提供标识之间的公共映射，排障人员仍需自行还原组件关系。

sections.title: 问题指向标识映射，具体实现仍待确认
paragraphs: 当前可核对的摘要内容主要解释了标识关联的缺口，未展开平台如何建立映射、如何处理采集数据。因此，这里不将问题描述扩写为已经得到证实的实现流程，也不据此绘制方法示意图。

sections.title: 跨层关联与单源归属都存在信息缺口
paragraphs: 摘要明确描述了两类障碍：跨来源时，关联一个 DU 事件、主机 CPU 峰值或交换机端口错误，需要针对每次查询手动重建拓扑；即使只看单一来源，指标携带的标识也不总能确定其所属组件或部署。

sections.title: 尚不能判断适用部署与验证范围

sections.title: 阅读启发：先确认数据能否关联，再讨论智能诊断
paragraphs: 阅读启发：面向智能运维，值得先追问指标能否明确归属到组件，以及跨层标识能否建立可靠联系。进一步阅读时，可重点查看论文如何定义和维护这些关系，以及用什么证据说明关联有效；不能仅因数据已被集中采集，就默认它们足以支持故障诊断。

papers.title: MODERN METHODS FOR PREDICTING THE REMAINING LIFE OF SHIP STRUCTURES
papers.abstract: The article examines modern methods for predicting the remaining life of metallic ship structures with due consideration of fatigue, crack growth, corrosion wastage, and actual operating conditions. The analytical basis comprises eleven peer-reviewed publications issued in 2021–2026 and three regulatory and technical documents published by IMO and DNV. Fracture mechanics, fatigue-life prediction, finite element analysis, corrosion prediction, structural health monitoring, and artificial-intelligence-based methods are compared. It is established that the reliability of a remaining-life assessment depends on the joint consideration of the measured structural condition, the model of subsequent degradation, future loading, and the applicable limit-state criterion. The most substantiated direction of further development is the integration of physics-based and probabilistic models with monitoring data and computational prediction tools.

papers.title: The influence of flow-field representation on electrical power and fatigue-load surrogate modelling in offshore wind farms
papers.abstract: High-fidelity aeroelastic simulations provide accurate predictions of electrical power and structural fatigue loads in wind farms but remain computationally expensive for optimisation, control, and digital-twin applications. Machine-learning surrogate models offer an efficient alternative, and recent studies have shown that both surrogate architecture and inflow representation influence predictive performance. However, it remains unclear how the amount and form of retained rotor-plane inflow information affect electrical power and fatigue-load prediction. This study evaluates four input configurations derived from temporally aggregated rotor-plane inflow data from the publicly available HAWC2Farm Lillgrund dataset. A minimal baseline representation retains only the spatial averages of the temporal-mean wind-speed and temporal-variance fields, while a flattened full-grid representation retains all rotor-plane measurements. Principal component analysis (PCA) provides a compact representation of the full input, and a two-dimensional representation preserves the original rotor-plane topology. The baseline, flattened, and PCA configurations are compared using the same SimpleMLP architecture under 5-fold GroupKFold cross-validation, while the two-dimensional spatial representation is evaluated separately using a convolutional neural network as a topology-aware modelling configuration. For electrical power prediction, the two-variable baseline already retained most of the predictive information, achieving an RMSE of approximately 2.2 % of rated power, while the distributed representations further reduced the absolute prediction error. For fatigue-load prediction, the effect of distributed inflow information was substantially more load-channel dependent, with only a marginal difference for tower-base fore–aft bending but much larger differences for blade-root edgewise and main-bearing bending. Within the fixed-architecture comparison, the PCA representation achieved the highest accuracy for electrical power prediction while reducing the input dimensionality from 1800 variables to 128 principal components. In contrast, the topology-aware CNN achieved the lowest prediction errors across all 12 fatigue-load components. These results show that the value of distributed rotor-plane information differs between the two prediction tasks and that the most effective representation–architecture configuration among those evaluated depends on the prediction objective.
